newsitem.title: TURKEY: Iraqi Kurd group says ceasefire ends after attack.
newsitem.headline: Iraqi Kurd group says ceasefire ends after attack.

text.p: An Iraqi Kurdish group said a nine-month-old ceasefire with a rival militia in northern Iraq had ended after the opposing group attacked its positions earlier this week.

The Kurdistan Democratic Party (KDP) said in a statement on Wednesday night that the Patritotic Union of Kurdistan (PUK) launched attacks on its bases on July 15-16 in Qasre region, near Iraq's border with Iran.
"This widespread attack...means the end of the ceasefire which so many hopes were built upon," the statement said.
The KDP of Massoud Barzani and Jalal Talabani's PUK have held several rounds of peace talks in Ankara following the U.S.-brokered ceasefire last October.
Many ceasefires between the two groups have been called and broken since the fighting first flared up in 1994.
The KDP joined with Iraqi troops to take control of the key Kurdish city of Arbil from Talabani's forces in fighting last August, prompting retaliatory U.S missile strikes on Iraqi targets.
The fighting gave Baghdad a foothold in northern Iraq for the first time since the end of the 1991 Gulf War when the Kurds broke away and set up their own administration under Western air power.
Two KDP militia members were killed and a further 14 wounded in this week's PUK attack, the statement said. It said Turkey's Kurdistan Workers Party (PKK) had fought alongside the PUK.
Turkey launched a large-scale cross border operation into northern Iraq against PKK hideouts in cooperation with Barzani's forces in May.
